newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell starts to clean up Nigerian oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Shell starts to clean up Nigerian oil spill.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Monday it was now cleaning up an oil spill at a site in the troubled Niger Delta where 1,000 youths rallied at the weekend to protest against oil firms.
"A contract to clean up the spill was signed last week and work has commenced," a Shell official in Lagos told Reuters.

The Saturday rally at the remote village of Aleibri in the Niger River Delta was called by activists demanding a better deal from oil companies and threatening possible violence if the multinationals do not comply.

Aleibri, to which the youths came by canoe from across oil-producing districts, was chosen as the meeting site because activists say Shell had refused to clear up a spill there on March 18, saying it was caused by sabotage.
The Shell official said there were good reasons for the delay in cleaning up the spill.

"This was partly because the community prevented access to the site to determine the cause of the spill and to clamp the hole," he said, adding "Ethnic clashes between Ijaws and Itsekiris in April, May and June caused further delay."

He said video and photo evidence of a joint investigation by the police, the department of petroleum resources, a community representative and Shell showed the spill was caused by sabotage when a hole was drilled in a pipeline.

Apart from Aleibri, the latest focus for campaigners has become four villages in the Delta where Shell has challenged a court ruling that it must pay 30 million naira ($360,000) for a spillage in 1982 which poisoned livestock and fishing grounds.
Shell has refused on the grounds that it does not pay compensation for cases caused by sabotage, and cannot set a precedent or other villagers will sabotage installations to get compensation money.

Shell pumps around half of Nigeria's over two million barrels per day crude oil production in a joint venture with state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp and is frequently the target of attack by neglected oil-producing communities.
